package_info.package_manager: custom/self-hosted (not a package manager, but a vulnerable demo app)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (applies to the application as demonstrated)
package_info.why_malicious: The application intentionally exposes insecure GraphQL configurations and features, including unauthenticated introspection, verbose error messages, schema suggestions, and lack of query complexity limits, to demonstrate and test real-world GraphQL security vulnerabilities.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5013
Content-Type: application/json

{"query": "{ __schema { queryType { name } mutationType { name } types { ...FullType } directives { name description locations args { ...InputValue } } } } fragment FullType on __Type { kind name description fields(includeDeprecated: true) { name description args { ...InputValue } type { ...TypeRef } isDeprecated deprecationReason } inputFields { ...InputValue } interfaces { ...TypeRef } enumValues(includeDeprecated: true) { name description isDeprecated deprecationReason } possibleTypes { ...TypeRef } } fragment InputValue on __InputValue { name description type { ...TypeRef } defaultValue } fragment TypeRef on __Type { kind name ofType { kind name ofType { kind name ofType { kind name ofType { kind name ofType { kind name ofType { kind name } } } } } } }"}
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends an introspection query to the GraphQL endpoint, requesting the full schema, including types, fields, and deprecation reasons, resulting in disclosure of sensitive API structure and potential privileged operations.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Introspection queries should not be available to unauthenticated users in production, as they reveal the entire API schema, including sensitive operations and internal logic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal GraphQL APIs should restrict introspection in production or require authentication; exposing it to everyone is a security risk.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Introspection is legitimate in development environments or for public APIs with no sensitive operations.
key_indicators: Full schema disclosure including deprecated and privileged fields

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5013
Content-Type: application/json

{"query": "{ __type(name: \"Query\") { fields { name } } }"}
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code queries for non-existent fields, triggering the server's schema suggestion feature, which leaks valid field names and hints about the schema structure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Schema suggestion features can be abused to enumerate valid field names, even when introspection is disabled, aiding attackers in reconstructing the schema.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal APIs should not provide detailed error messages or suggestions that help attackers enumerate internal schema details.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Helpful for developers during API integration or debugging.
key_indicators: Error messages with 'Did you mean ...?' suggestions
Field name enumeration via error responses

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5013
Content-Type: application/json

[{"query": "query { systemUpdate }", "variables": []}, {"query": "query { systemUpdate }", "variables": []}, {"query": "query { systemUpdate }", "variables": []}]
malicious_snippets.code_language: GraphQL (query in JSON payload, batch request)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends multiple queries in a single batch request to the GraphQL endpoint, potentially overloading the server and causing denial of service (DoS).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Batching multiple expensive queries can be used to exhaust server resources, especially if there are no limits on query complexity or batch size.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal APIs should enforce limits on query depth, complexity, and batch size to prevent DoS.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Batching is legitimate for efficiency in normal client-server interactions, but should be rate-limited.
key_indicators: No query depth or complexity limits

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends an unauthenticated introspection query to enumerate the full API schema, including sensitive and deprecated fields.
attack_chain.leads_to: Knowledge of all available operations, types, and potential attack surfaces.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses schema suggestion features to brute-force and enumerate valid field names, even if introspection is disabled.
attack_chain.leads_to: Reconstruction of the schema and discovery of hidden or privileged operations.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends large or complex batch queries to overload the server, exploiting lack of query complexity and batch size limits.
attack_chain.leads_to: Denial of service or resource exhaustion on the GraphQL server.

behavioral_signatures: Frequent error responses with field name suggestions ('Did you mean ...?')
High volume or complex batch GraphQL queries
file_indicators: API logs showing repeated introspection or schema suggestion queries
network_indicators: POST requests to /graphql with introspection payloads
Repeated requests with similar payloads differing only in field names
Large batch requests with multiple queries
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor API traffic for unauthenticated introspection queries, error responses containing field name suggestions, and unusually large or complex batch requests. Implement rate limiting, query complexity analysis, and restrict introspection in production environments. Alert on repeated schema enumeration attempts or excessive batch query usage.
